t: problem: users are querying too many starred repos (some users have tens of thousands of repos starred) - we should implement a cached list of repos that have been detected by users as implementing the open session license (with a server side check, at most once daily per repo). Instead of a user making the query to all the repos, they make one query to our hosted repo list with their list of starred repos, and we return the ones in that list that have been known to implement the license. Propose a pattern to solve this if you can come up with a better one. repo id is the canonical key. Perhaps we present the user the list of their starred repos for them to decide to follow, isntead of forcing them to follow each repo. also simply entering a repo name or url to follow to add it to their following list

Proposed registry pattern: hosted registry keyed by GitHub repo id, server-side verification, follows as opt-in curated list, manual follow by name/URL, plus (initially) a global daily code-search sweep and registry-as-feed-backbone.
I like the shape of the api suggestion, but the nightly sweep feels excessive. Perhaps we only sweep as users submit their list of starred repos, rechecking only once each day

Built the demand-driven registry: opensession-api Lambda (API + SQS worker in one) on the existing gateway under /api; DynamoDB opensession-repos (PK repoId), opensession-follows (userId/repoId), opensession-authcache (token-hash to GitHub user, 1h TTL); SQS opensession-verify queue with worker concurrency 2. Verification is a HEAD on raw.githubusercontent.com (no GitHub API quota), enforced at most once daily per repo by the worker; repos enter the queue only when users match starred lists or submit a repo. Endpoints: POST /api/repos/match (batch intersect + queue unknown/stale), POST /api/repos/submit (resolve with caller token, verify inline, auto-follow), GET/PUT/DELETE /api/follows. Client reworked: registry.ts client, Feed now shows opt-in Following section (live-polls only follows), From-your-stars discovery scanned in 1000-star windows with scan-more, and follow-by-name/URL box. Smoke-tested the full loop live (queue to verified to active; 422 for non-adopters). 15 tests green; deployed to production.

t: after loading the site I am not seeing a searchable display area for my starred repos I might want to follow which have the turn history artifact. Also a separate issue to consider - is there a way to pull the delta on the jsonl from the previous loaded version so we do not have to pull the full file? since it is append only, we would only need to get the turns since the last time we queried it

Two fixes. (1) From-your-stars is now a searchable browser: search box over all scanned stars, per-repo state badges (open session / verifying / no session artifact) powered by a new inactive field in the match response, results capped at 50 with refine hint, and pending repos re-matched every 15s so worker verdicts appear live without reload. (2) Delta fetching: history files are append-only, so opens now probe the blob sha/size, then issue an HTTP Range request for only the appended bytes with a 64-byte overlap check (byte-accurate, multibyte-safe); overlap mismatch or CDN staleness falls back to a full fetch, and per-repo text is cached in localStorage (512KB cap). 21 tests green; deployed.
